title: Repeated marks in one stage, with packed certificates
description: Proves the all-moduli Dirichlet boundary 2186813/2500000 = 0.8747252, with the principal pole excluded. The proof is the repeated-marks proof (arvi-repeated-marks-20261024) run as a single stage, plus faster certificates. (1) The natural cost is K = 9/2 = 6(2·7/8 − 1). The cap 6(2β − 1) ≤ K, which the source step and the final return need, is then the baseline's own theorem β ≤ 7/8. Collet's seed step, his intermediate return and the re-proof of PR 67 are therefore no longer in the proof, and the closure of the bound loses about 37% of its export bytes (4.3 GB to 2.7 GB). (2) The face family starts on Collet's natural face GlobalSource 1 (9/2) (11/200), which his natural source theorem accepts for every K between 21/5 and 9/2. It is regenerated for K = 9/2, with breakpoints 0.0122820, 0.01942, 0.0252, 0.0310, 0.0367 and 0.0424122. Its end faces do not depend on the seed, so the final return, regenerated with 32 rows and 9 windows, closes at 2186813/2500000. (3) The HIGH-gate and special-sector certificates are computed in packed integer arithmetic. Every polynomial is carried as a few big numbers (A(X), B(X), A(1), B(1)) for natural coefficient lists A and B, scaled by a power of a common denominator. The packed formula is proved to represent the rational one and is checked once against literal integer data. The Bernstein trees and interval tests then run on that data. An interval test reads the shifted coefficients directly as base-Y digits of the packed number, with Y = 2^e X − k. Kernel time of these certificates falls from about 2600 s to about 170 s. The analytic estimates are Collet's and the baseline's, imported unchanged. The research, drafting and Lean development were AI-assisted.
